title: Rising Prices Have People in Japan Dining Out Less
paragraphs: A meal at a restaurant means no cooking and no dishes to wash. But these days, more people in Japan seem to think the price may not be worth it.

A new survey by kitchen appliance maker Tiger Corporation found that 62% of people now eat at home more often and dine out less. Among them, 65% said rising prices had made them cut back on restaurant spending.
The survey, which included over 600 adults, also found that 90% felt their food costs had increased in recent years.

And they're not wrong. More than 20,000 food and drink items in Japan have risen in price or are set to rise in 2026 alone, according to research company Teikoku Databank. It is the second year in a row that the number has passed 20,000.
But saving money is not the only reason people are eating at home more — one in five said it felt more relaxing and comfortable.
When asked what they hoped to gain from eating at home, 45% of people said better value for money than dining out. Convenience came next at 37%, followed by nutrition at 35%.
And while people might be less willing to spend money eating out these days, just over half said they wanted to buy kitchen appliances to improve their meals at home.
After all, doing the dishes might not seem so bad if the meal was great!
